title: Coupling Between Dendritic Arborization and Intrinsic Membrane Physiology in the Released Mouse and Human Reconstructions of the Allen Cell Types Database
content: How much physiological information does the geometry of a cortical neuron's dendritic arbor carry, and does the answer differ between mouse and human? We re-derived arborization morphometrics for all 701 three-dimensional reconstructions in the Allen Cell Types Database (537 mouse, 164 human), validated the re-derivation against the released summaries, and linked morphology to intrinsic physiology cell by cell, treating the donor - not the cell - as the unit of inference. Coupling between total dendritic length and input resistance was negative in both released samples but far stronger among the human reconstructions (rho = -0.87, 95% CI -0.91 to -0.80; n = 162 cells, 35 donors) than among the mouse reconstructions (rho = -0.25, CI -0.38 to -0.12; n = 236 cells, 163 donors). Distribution matching and common-support restriction attenuate roughly half of the species contrast in Fisher-z units, while direct donor-aware contrasts at the shared restriction confirm that a substantial residual difference remains (Fisher-z difference -0.42 to -0.57; all intervals exclude zero), with wide uncertainty at the strictest restriction (human -0.67; n = 49 cells, 18 donors). Under comparable sampling distributions, the mouse gain in prediction from arbor geometry beyond size (+0.34) fell to +0.03 to +0.06 within mouse excitatory cells, and the human value (-0.05) was not stable under restriction; apical predominance was not supported. These findings quantify how sampling composition and morphological range shape species differences in this release; the residual coupling-magnitude contrast remains an observational comparison between released samples that differ in preparation and size range. Reproducible analysis code is openly archived with the study.
